content: We need number of carbonyl (C=O) groups in the sample's molecule. We have no direct description of molecule. We can use IR spectra to detect carbonyl stretch, or carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbons (~190-220 ppm). Use IR spectra tool (cheapest?). Both carbon NMR and IR are single measurement. Probably IR is cheaper? Both cost similar. Use IR to see C=O stretch peaks around 1700 cm-1. Let's get IR.
